headline: GALENA STRIKES AGAIN: AMERICAS GOLD DRILLS 1,062 G/T Ag IN NEW VEIN; CRESCENT HITS 1,891 G/T Ag ON SAME DAY
snippet: Americas Gold and Silver (TSX: USA) reported September 18 that its record 2026 exploration program at the Galena Complex in Idaho's Coeur d'Alene district has intersected a new Galena Mine vein grading 1,062 g/t Ag and 0.7% Cu over 1.3 metres while Crescent Mine drilling simultaneously returned 1,891 g/t Ag and 0.3% Cu over 1.3 metres — infill drilling across the complex is also outperforming the currently modelled Mineral Resource with grades higher than the existing block model, and the company has announced it will conduct its largest-ever exploration program in 2026 following these back-to-back high-grade vein discoveries.

headline: GOLD EXTENDS POST-FED CLIMB TO $4,385 — BUYERS RETURN AS OIL RETREATS AND RATE-HIKE ANXIETY FADES
snippet: Spot gold advanced to approximately US$4,385 per ounce on September 18 — up roughly $40 from Thursday's post-FOMC close — as dip buyers returned and a softening crude-oil tape reduced the session's inflation premium; Comex gold settled $4,360 on September 17 as investors began distinguishing between the Fed's past-tense quarter-point hike and the now-contested odds of the next move, with 16 of 18 FOMC participants having pencilled in at least one more increase before year-end but rate futures markets pricing the probability below 55%.

headline: GROUP ELEVEN'S BALLYWIRE GERMANIUM GRADES JUMP 68% ON BETTER ASSAY — IRELAND DISCOVERY JUST GOT BIGGER
snippet: Group Eleven Resources (TSXV: ZNG) announced September 17 that 220 re-analysed drill-core samples from five Ballywire holes using a new fusion assay method returned germanium grades averaging 68% higher than original readings — one 8-metre interval jumped from 8.9 g/t to 25 g/t Ge, with peak values up to 95 g/t Ge; a standout re-assayed interval returned 29.9 metres at 15.3% Zn+Pb, 552 g/t Ag, 0.67% Cu and 16 g/t Ge, including 8.4 metres at 18.2% Zn+Pb, 1,776 g/t Ag, 2.21% Cu and 25 g/t Ge. The grade upgrade is permanent: the old lithium borate fusion method systematically volatilised germanium as GeCl4, so grades were always present but never accurately measured; four drill rigs remain active at Ballywire, described as Ireland's most significant mineral discovery in over a decade.

headline: FATHOM NICKEL FINDS NEW Ni-Cu-Co ZONES BEYOND GOCHAGER LAKE MRE — TARGET CORRIDOR EXTENDS ON STRIKE AND DEPTH
snippet: Fathom Nickel (CSE: FNI) announced September 16 that drilling west-southwest and east-northeast of its Gochager Lake Ni-Cu-Co Deposit in Saskatchewan has intersected new zones of Gochager-style disseminated sulphide mineralization, including local semi-massive to massive vein and breccia zones — standout hole GL26029 cut 21.44 metres of mineralized core with greater-than 1% Ni in a new target to the southwest; the discovery of additional zones comes six days after Fathom's September 10 maiden MRE of 3.1 million inferred tonnes at 0.45% NiEq, suggesting that resource-estimate contained only a fraction of the broader 8-km nickel-copper-cobalt trend.

headline: MAGNUM MINING COMPLETES 10,000M AUGER PROGRAM AT AZIMUTH — JORC REE RESOURCE DUE NOVEMBER, 94% EXTRACTION RECOVERIES
snippet: Magnum Mining and Exploration (ASX: MGU) confirmed September 18 that its 10,000-metre auger drilling programme at the Piracanjuba North Project in Goiás, Brazil is complete, with 10,313.97 metres across 867 collars — 7,137 metres focused on the Plateau Zone, a single ionic-adsorption-clay (IAC) domain covering approximately 32.5 km²; grades reach up to 3,971 ppm TREO with desorption recoveries up to 94% MREO, positioning the project against a previously defined 700–1,200 Mt exploration target; a JORC Mineral Resource Estimate is targeted by November 2026, adding a non-Chinese IAC deposit to the list of supply alternatives as the China rare-earth export-control clock ticks toward its November 10 expiry.

headline: GOLDSEEK: AUTUMN SEASONALITY FAVORS GOLD STOCKS — GDX HISTORICALLY PEAKS LATE SEPTEMBER, ANALYSTS FLAG 20–30% MINER UPSIDE
snippet: In the latest Zeal LLC seasonal analysis published on GoldSeek, gold stocks have entered their historically strongest window of the year: the autumn rally that typically runs from late August through late September has historically delivered 10%+ moves in physical gold and 20–30% gains in major gold miners through the GDX operating-leverage multiplier; the piece notes that summer 2026's anomalous selling — driven by new Fed Chair Warsh's hawkishness and broad uncertainty — set up a potential compression buy as the FOMC decision is now priced and miners approach their 12th consecutive quarter of record earnings growth.

headline: COPPER TARIFF CLOCK RUNS: COMEX HITS RECORD 695,624-TONNE STOCKPILE AS TRUMP DECISION STAYS 2+ MONTHS OVERDUE
snippet: Copper extended losses near US$14,200 per tonne on the LME this week as traders continue front-running an anticipated 15% US tariff on refined copper imports — a Commerce Department report that was due two months ago and has yet to be published — driving Comex warehouse inventories to a record 695,624 tonnes, more than double the combined LME and Shanghai stocks; while the US stockpile has exploded, Shanghai inventories stand at just 63,000 tonnes, their lowest since January 2024, creating a two-speed market that underscores the global copper supply shortage beneath the tariff arbitrage noise.

headline: UBS: GOLD VOLATILITY LIKELY NEAR-TERM BUT 12-MONTH OUTLOOK CONSTRUCTIVE — STRATEGIC ALLOCATION BUY ZONE
snippet: UBS analysts flagged near-term gold price volatility as likely given the Fed's signalling of at least one more quarter-point hike before year-end and elevated real yields, but maintained a constructive 12-month outlook underpinned by continued central-bank buying, fiscal deficit concerns, and de-dollarisation demand that is structurally independent of the rate cycle; the note comes days after UBS raised its Newmont price target to $155 and is viewed by gold market watchers as an implicit signal that the recent pullback from all-time highs above $5,600 to the $4,300–$4,400 zone represents a strategic re-entry window.

headline: INDIA'S FESTIVE GOLD SEASON STARTS WITH CAUTIOUS OPTIMISM — JEWELLERS REBUILD INVENTORY BELOW $4,500 PRICE POINT
snippet: India's gold jewellery trade is entering the festive season — spanning Navratri through Diwali — with cautious optimism according to the latest GoldSeek market update; dealers are rebuilding inventory at current sub-$4,500 levels ahead of the high-demand October–November window, though price sensitivity remains elevated among retail buyers and jewellers are hedging at shorter forward horizons than in prior years; India consumed a record 797 tonnes of gold in 2025 and the World Gold Council expects the 2026 run-rate to stay above 750 tonnes despite higher prices.

headline: LITHIUM MARKET BIFURCATES: PRICES UP 81% YEAR-ON-YEAR BUT FELL 13% IN AUGUST — ENERGY STORAGE DEMAND vs CHINA OVERSUPPLY
snippet: Lithium carbonate pricing on the Wuhan exchange rose 0.76% on September 17 to 133,200 CNY/tonne, but the metal is still 13% below its August peak despite being up 81% year-over-year as Chinese spodumene concentrate production and emerging-market battery-grade supply weigh on near-term spot prices; Sprott's latest sector analysis argues that this price volatility obscures a structural demand inflection — global lithium demand through May 2026 jumped 45% year-on-year, battery energy storage systems now account for a larger share of consumption than EVs in some monthly datasets, and US and European policy support is accelerating non-Chinese processing capacity.

headline: GOLD PRICE FORECAST ROUNDUP: J.P. MORGAN TARGETS $6,000 BY Q4, KITCO MEDIAN AT $4,509 — BIGGEST RANGE IN A DECADE
snippet: September 2026 gold price forecasts now span the widest range in a decade: J.P. Morgan maintains a $6,000/oz Q4 target citing dollar erosion, central bank accumulation above 1,000 tonnes for a fourth consecutive year, and Middle East risk premium, while the Kitco analyst-survey median sits at $4,509/oz and conservative models place a floor at $4,136; working consensus clusters between $4,500 and $4,900 by year-end, but the divergence itself signals structural uncertainty — the same fiscal and geopolitical drivers that lifted gold 67% in 2025 are still active while the Fed's hawkish tilt adds a headwind not present during last year's bull run.
